messages:
maya.docs: Heads-up I'm opening a small PR to clarify Dedicated provisioning wording + add a CLI validation example. looking for one reviewer for YAML correctness and one for link hygiene.
jon.eng: can do a quick YAML skim. where will the CLI snippet live? top of the quickstart or a new 'validation' subsection?
maya.docs: planned under quickstart as "validation and linting" so people see it early. snippet will show `redwoodctl validate` and `redwoodctl lint` examples.
tara.sre: +1 on making validation prominent. also please include a note about how validation differs for private deployments (offline KMS checks not performed).
olivia.devex: ping me once you have the SDK call snippet. I'll run it against our example YAMLs. small ask: please use the exact field names from the API (we've had drift on `isolation_required` vs `requires_isolation`).
maya.docs: good catch. I'll canonicalize to `requires_isolation`. updated the example: ```yaml
provisioningPolicy:
  name: standard-dedicated
  minInstances: 1
  maxInstances: 8
  requires_isolation: false
  autoscale:
    policy: conservative
    cooldown_sec: 90
```
jon.eng: looks consistent. question: earlier examples used `minPods`/`maxPods` in runtime docs. do we want `minInstances` everywhere or leave a migration note?
maya.docs: adding a migration note mapping `minPods->minInstances` and `maxPods->maxInstances` with a tiny transform. will link to the migration guide.
tara.sre: add a short sentence under SLAs: "If minInstances cannot be met due to capacity, traffic is queued with soft-degrade; if queue time > 10s then traffic will route to fallback model variant." This helps oncall know expected behaviors.
olivia.devex: SDK snippet (python) looks like this — I'll paste and run in a sec: ```python
from redwood_sdk import ProvisioningClient
client = ProvisioningClient()
client.validate_policy('path/to/policy.yaml')
```
link-bot: link-checker: scanned PR branch -> found 2 relative links to `../old-handbook` that 404.
maya.docs: thanks bot. fixing links now to point to `/handbook/provisioning` and adding redirect note.
junior.docs: tiny nit from my review: use backticks for field names and surround CLI examples with single-line code blocks for readability.
maya.docs: fixed both. also added a short "bulk onboarding" example to illustrate cooldown interplay (large ramp from 2->50 nodes).
omittedUser: does the quick example mention bursting policy and reserved capacity behavior? we should document how reserved capacity reserves instances vs autoscale.
maya.docs: added a two-sentence note: reserved pools guarantee capacity at commit and bypass the normal preemption path; autoscale still applies to non-reserved tenants.
jon.eng: LGTM for YAML. olivia, can you sanity-check SDK call responses? if you add expected error examples (invalid label, missing key) that's useful for users.
olivia.devex: will add expected error payloads and run tests. will report back in this thread. :eyes: 
maya.docs: thanks everyone. pushing PR in ~15m; will tag reviewers and include `redwoodctl validate --file provisioning-example.yaml` in the quickstart.
